findings.claim: The migration treats any stat failure as 'file absent', so a stat error other than not-found empties the pointer of a row whose picture still exists.
findings.impact: A permission or I/O error on the cache at the first startup empties those pointers silently, and the run counts them as `emptied`, not `failed`. The old files stay at paths no row names, and the next run has nothing to retry. A `.loft` then needs Refresh metadata and loses its picture for good if the remote one has gone. It needs a faulty cache mount at upgrade time, so it is not ordinary use.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/thumbnail.py:707-710 returns ("absent", rel) on any OSError. thumbnail.py:793-798 then repoints or empties the row. The spec's grouping and I10 speak of a file that does not exist, while I9 keeps the pointer only when os.replace fails.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. By reading: make `<thumbs>/<drive>` unsearchable before startup, and stat raises PermissionError for each row under it, so a sole-owner row with no slot gets an empty pointer.

bucket_proposal.reason: A cache mount failing at the upgrade is outside normal use and no declared invariant covers a stat error. It still reads wrong because retryable failures are handled destructively.

findings.proposed_fix: Treat only FileNotFoundError and NotADirectoryError as absent. For any other OSError, keep the pointer, log a warning and count the row as failed, as I9 does for os.replace.

specification_compliance: Answer to the first-review question: the diff reaches four places outside the touch-point list: docs/developer-guide/architecture.md (TP-1), the allow-list in backend/tests/test_atomic_write.py (TP-2), the rewritten assertion in test_transparent_thumbnails.py (TP-3) and the inverted assertion in test_copy.py (TP-4).
backend/tests/test_thumbnail_slots.py is new and not named, but it falls under the `backend/tests/` touch point and carries the spec's invariant tests, so I did not raise it.

The six deleted tests match the spec's list exactly. test_scanner_move_detection is the one listed rewrite. The changes in test_upload.py and the two `endswith` assertions in test_transparent_thumbnails.py only change expected path values.
_is_flattened_transparent_picture keeps its check of other rows, as spec section 7 requires. Only its docstring changed, so I raised nothing.

Read against the code, the core invariants I1-I14 and I16-I21 hold. I15's migration half holds. Its Media Import half is not in this commit: addons/media_import/backend/service.py:606-622 still writes the path form, which the Delivery section expects for the old pin.

Submodules: no addon or test imports the removed path_thumbnail_rel, _move_thumbnail, _relocate_thumbnail or _expected_thumbnail_path, and no addon calls resolve_db_path_conflict. Media Import's register_single_file callers register .loft files, which have no generator, so no slot is written for them there.

Persistence: _set_pointer holds updated_at (thumbnail.py:727). Renames commit every 200 rows, and an uncommitted rename is repointed on the next run through the absent-file-with-slot branch. A shared group commits its emptied pointers before unlinking.

Concurrency: main.py:276-280 awaits the migration before the scan task, addon startup and yield. The Dockerfile starts uvicorn with one worker, so two migrations cannot race. The batch routers roll back on every exception (routers/files.py:368, 373, 509, 519), so a flushed ghost delete cannot ride out on the next file's commit, and I13's failure half holds for batches.
potential_unspecified_behavior: A stat error other than not-found counts as an absent file during migration (MIG-1).

Two rows naming one absent path string form a shared group and are both emptied, even if each has a slot file, whereas I10's wording repoints a row with an existing slot. I found no ordinary way to reach this: a shared group commits its emptied pointers before unlinking, so a stopped run cannot produce it. An existing slot would be stranded, and a .loft would lose its picture.

A scan-detected move of a row with an empty or dangling .by-id pointer no longer generates in that scan, because _relocate_thumbnail is gone. The placeholder stays until the next scan. This agrees with I3 and I16, but the spec does not state the one-scan delay.
regression_risks: prune_empty_dirs and physical_delete's _cleanup_empty_parents can remove .by-id when its last slot goes. A generator between _atomic's mkdir and mkstemp would then get FileNotFoundError, and in a scan that is uncaught. The window is very narrow and needs a nearly empty cache.

The old-pin delivery window: the decisions record shows Media Import's 30-second caption retry rewriting .loft rows to path form with a new mtime and ETag, and each later startup moves them again until the addon PR lands. The spec expects this, but it means I7's same-ETag result does not hold across that retry.

Grouping relies on st_dev and st_ino being stable and unique on the cache mount. A mount that reuses inode numbers would treat sole owners as shared and delete their pictures. The recorded Compose upgrade shows the expected counts on the one mount it ran on.
test_coverage: Covered by read tests: I1, I2, I3 (all operations and types, including scan-detected moves), I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I12, I16, I19, I20 and I21, plus the path-form selection part of I11 and the migration half of I15.
Gap: I13 for rename and copy (TEST-1). I13's failure half is tested only for a move.
Gap: I11's second half, a projection serving after its source migrates with no re-copy, has no automated test. It rests on the preserved mtime tested under I7 and on the manual run in decisions.md.
Gap: I14 is tested only for a Missing row, not an Active row whose file vanished. Both take the same branch in upload.py:307.
Gap: the spec's failure case 'upload with a new id, the commit fails: the slot is removed' (upload.py:360-362) has no test I could find in test_upload.py or test_thumbnail_slots.py.
I18 asserts only thumbnail_path, not the whole field set, but routers/internal.py is unchanged.
